summary: The paper studies gate-based quantum generative models for copula learning on Indian stock market returns, using a 6-qubit, 8-layer QGAN and QCBM variants evaluated on 1000 bootstrapped samples with KS and E-statistics. Reported KS ranges are 0.0418-0.0458 for QGAN, 0.0385-0.0460 for QCBM-Regular, 0.0398-0.0452 for QCBM-Annealing, and 0.0414-0.0590 for QCBM-Genetic, compared with 0.0416-0.0443 for the classical Student-t copula baseline.

experiments.description: Quantum Generative Adversarial Network (QGAN) used to learn a copula distribution for Indian stock market indices, evaluated with different binning strategies and compared against a classical parametric Student-t copula.

algorithm.variant: QGAN with fully quantum generator and MPS quantum discriminator
algorithm.ansatz: Generator circuit with maximally entangled initial state and layers of RZ, RX, and RZZ gates; discriminator is an MPS circuit

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Continuous copula samples are discretized into binary strings; for a 6-qubit circuit, each of the 2 variables is represented by 3 qubits (3 bits per variable), producing 64 bins total
problem_formulation.objective_function: Adversarially learn the target discrete distribution corresponding to the copula-transformed market data
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No explicit constraints beyond the copula-space discretization and adversarial training

problem_instance.description: Modeling dependence structure between NIFTY 50 and NIFTY BANK returns in copula space

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: closing prices converted to returns; returns mapped to copula space using probability integral transform; continuous values discretized via binning strategy; generated binary samples inverse-transformed back to continuous space
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Each model run 5 times with different random initializations; for each run, 5 sets of 1000 samples were drawn from the trained circuit; KS statistic and E-statistic computed against 1000 bootstrapped real samples; only p-value < 0.05 results retained
